I have done a bunch of research and cannot find one case of a hosting provider being sued for taking down a website. After reading a few of the hosting agreements, I can see why: Generally the most you can recover are the fees that were paid. The actual fine print reads:

IN ADDITION, You SPECIFICALLY ACKNOWLEDGE AND agree that in no event shall [Hosting Provider's] total aggregate liability exceed the total amount paid by you for the particular ServiceS that ARE the subject of the cause of action."

So, at the end of the day, they MIGHT be able to get their fees back, but this would, in no way, be even close to the cost of the lawyer.

As far as the illegal content posted, they are required by law (in the US) to report it to the FBI and provide any assistance necessary to help identify and locate the offending party(s). And to avoid getting in trouble themselves, will immediately take down a site with, even suspected illegal content so there is not question that they were not involved with the dissemination. Better to get sued for pennies, then go to jail for not taking down the site.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not defending the behavior of the provider, just supplying a context.
